newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe confidence vote set for October 2.
newsitem.headline: Juppe confidence vote set for October 2.

text.p: A parliamentary vote of confidence in French Prime Minister Alain Juppe's economic policies will be held on October 2, parliamentary sources said on Wednesday.
Juppe on Tuesday called the vote, the third since he came to office in May 1995, in an effort to outflank critics of austerity within his fractious centre-right coalition.
Juppe will make a speech to the National Assembly to outline his government's economic policies at 4 p.m. (1400 GMT) next Wednesday and then ask for a vote of confidence, the sources said.
Several coalition politicians have criticised planned income tax cuts as inadequate and sought a change in economic policy to boost sluggish growth and combat 12.5 percent unemployment.
Parliament reconvenes after the summer recess next Tuesday. Since the coalition holds four-fifths of the 577 assembly seats, the outcome of the vote is a foregone conclusion.
